standard.title: Create and edit literary texts
standard.description: create and edit literary texts that experiment with language features and literary devices for particular purposes and effects
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create literary texts that use language features and literary devices to create character, setting and mood (AC9E7LE06). They have not yet focused on deliberate experimentation — using devices with conscious intentionality toward a particular effect — or on collaborative and iterative editing of literary writing with peer feedback.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create and edit literary texts that experiment with language features and literary devices for particular purposes and effects.

nodes.label: Experimenting with language features and devices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a literary text that deliberately experiments with at least one language feature or literary device, and articulate the purpose or effect the experiment is intended to achieve.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a short literary piece (e.g. a short story opening or poem) that deliberately uses at least one literary device or language feature for a named effect, and explain the choice made.
nodes.typical_width: Create literary texts that combine multiple literary devices (e.g. imagery, tone, dialogue choices) to achieve a specific purpose or evoke a specific reader response; make deliberate and reflective choices in the writing process.
wider: Create a short story with a sustained use of a single dominant device (e.g. extended metaphor or unreliable narrator perspective) and reflect on how the constraint shaped the writing
Collaborate with a peer to write a short script focusing on dialogue choices for each character, and reflect on how the dialogue reveals character through language rather than description

Experiment with combining literary devices from different cultural traditions (e.g. First Nations storytelling features with Western narrative conventions) to create a distinctive hybrid literary text

response_modes.reason: Literary experimentation requires a repertoire of devices to experiment with. Students who have only analysed devices need guided practice deploying them in their own writing across multiple short tasks before the experimental relationship to craft becomes comfortable.

success_criteria: Creates a literary text that uses at least one named literary device or language feature deliberately.
Can explain the purpose or intended effect of the device choice in their own text.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 is editing for effect — a task that requires students to have a created text to edit and, crucially, to have made deliberate device choices in that text to revisit and evaluate. Students who have not built a working repertoire at Node 1 produce undifferentiated writing with no purposeful choices to reflect on or revise.

nodes.label: Editing for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit their own literary texts — revising imagery, word choices and structural features — and reflect on how editing decisions change the effect of the text.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit one piece of own literary writing by revising at least one imagery choice or word choice and explain how the revision changes the intended effect.
nodes.typical_width: Edit literary texts with attention to imagery, word choices and structural features; reflect on how editing decisions affect the overall purpose and effect; use peer feedback to inform editing choices.
wider: Conduct a sustained editing cycle on a longer literary piece — draft, peer review, revise, reflect — documenting how the text changed and why each revision decision was made
Compare the draft and final versions of a published author's work (where available) to examine how editing decisions changed the effect of the text
Edit a collaborative script written with a peer, focusing on ensuring each character's dialogue is consistent and distinct in voice

response_modes.reason: Editing literary writing requires students to hold their authorial intention and the reader's experience simultaneously — seeing the text from outside themselves. This integration of compositional and reader perspectives is the hardest part of the creative editing process and warrants explicit attention.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The iterative writing and editing cycle — particularly with collaborative peer review — is rich territory for building genuine craft awareness. Students who engage deeply with the revision process develop a qualitatively different relationship to language choices than those who draft once and submit.
success_criteria: Produces a revised version of a literary text with at least one deliberate and explainable change to imagery, word choice or structure.
Articulates how the revision changes or improves the intended effect of the text.
